title: github-actions-templates Review: Build-and-Deploy Templates, Nothing for Scheduled Jobs
description: We asked this skill for a weekly scheduled check of our live site. It has no scheduled pattern, and its three template files are missing upstream. Its security basics carried over, and the finished job found a real problem on the first run.

author.name: TrustedSkills Team
author.bio: We assess AI agent skills by installing them, running them against real work, and reading the source. We don't accept payment for reviews.

basisNote: Part of a batch of thirteen data and automation skills run on the same day against the same dataset: this site's own registry index, 26,001 skills in one 71 MB JSON file. Each run worked in its own private copy of the site's repository. One run on one dataset is one data point, not a benchmark.

runs.task: Add a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that checks the live site weekly and fails loudly. Do not duplicate the existing daily rebuild. Use only the repo's own read-only checks, follow the skill's templates and security advice, lint the workflow with actionlint, and run the chosen checks locally once. Do not push.
runs.outcome:
`npx skills add wshobson/agents --skill github-actions-templates` installed it first time.

The skill has no pattern for this job. Its examples (test, Docker build and push, Kubernetes deploy, matrix build, security scan, approval gates) all run on push, pull request or tag. None uses `on: schedule`. The agent wrote the schedule trigger from general knowledge.

Three times the skill says "See `assets/...`" for a full template. There is no `assets` folder in the install or in the upstream repository.

Two of its best practices carried over: fixed action versions (`@v4`, not `@latest`) and the smallest permissions (`contents: read`). The agent skipped dependency caching because the check needs no install. The result is a short weekly job with a 5-minute timeout. actionlint reported no problems.

Run locally, the chosen check failed against the live site: a skill page's canonical tag pointed at the home page. We confirmed it with curl. The fix already exists in our code and was waiting to be deployed, so the job caught a real gap between the code and the live site on its first run.
runs.environment: Claude Code subagent (Sonnet 5) with the installed SKILL.md loaded as its instructions, in a private clone of the TrustedSkills website repo at commit 5169470. actionlint 1.7.12 release binary.

summary: A set of CI/CD templates for container apps: test, build, push, deploy to Kubernetes, scan. If that is your job, the patterns are reasonable. For anything else, such as a scheduled check or report, it has nothing, and the full templates it points to do not exist. Its short best-practices list is the part that transferred.

strengths.title: Sound security basics
strengths.body: Fixed action versions and minimal permissions are in its best-practice list, and both went into our workflow.

strengths.title: Reasonable build-and-deploy patterns
strengths.body: Matrix builds, Docker metadata, environment approvals and a reusable workflow example.

strengths.title: Plain YAML any agent can use
strengths.body: Nothing in it depends on one agent or editor.

limitations.title: No scheduled workflows
limitations.body: No example uses `on: schedule` or cron, though scheduled jobs are a common reason to write a workflow.

limitations.title: Three dead template links
limitations.body: It refers to `assets/test-workflow.yml` and two other files that do not exist, upstream or installed.

limitations.title: Pins to tags, not commits
limitations.body: It recommends `@v4` over `@latest`, but not pinning third-party actions to a commit SHA.

bestFor.title: Container build and deploy pipelines
bestFor.body: Write scheduled and maintenance jobs from GitHub's own docs instead.

notFor: Scheduled checks, reports or other automation that is not build and deploy.
